title: Is the Agent Harness Dead? — Jediah Katz, SpaceXAI
talk_summary: A Cursor/SpaceX harness engineer argues that coding-specific harness tricks (prompt scaffolding, edit-application models, codebase-exploration instructions) are being absorbed by smarter models, but the harness still matters for cost/efficiency, trust/security, and long-running cloud infrastructure. He describes concrete mechanisms: a central registry of deterministic 'shims' that auto-PR themselves for deletion when they stop firing, event 'subscriptions' as a composable primitive, and cost tuning via cache hit rate, token efficiency, and model mix.

takeaways.technique: Efficiency tuning as a first-class harness workstream (cache hit rate, token efficiency, model mix)
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly optimize the harness for cost and latency without quality loss by tweaking cache hit rate, token efficiency, and which model handles which step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: through tweaking variables like uh cache hit rate, improving that, token efficiency, um model mix, we were able to bring down the costs and the speed
takeaways.numbers: no specific figures cited; claims 'significantly' lower cost and faster with 'no hit to quality'

takeaways.what_they_do: Deterministic guardrails/hacks that patch model misbehavior are tracked centrally and logged each time they fire; a bot watches the dashboard and opens a PR to delete a shim once it stops firing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we track all these things, which we call shims centrally, and every time the model uses one, it gets logged... whenever a shim stops firing, that model or that agent will put up a PR and say this shim can be cleaned up

takeaways.technique: Event 'subscriptions' as a single composable primitive
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of separate integrations per event source, one framework/tool lets agents subscribe to events (Slack post, CI red on a PR, time of day) and wake on them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: rather than having one separate integration, you know, having separate integrations for each of these things, we have one framework and one tool that the model can use

takeaways.technique: Long-running work must run off the laptop / in cloud
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue multi-hour-to-multi-day agent tasks cannot run on a machine that sleeps; the runtime must be cloud-hosted with resumable state.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's just no way that this can work on one person's laptop, which might go to sleep. It has to be running in the cloud

takeaways.technique: Scoped permissions and spend guardrails per agent
takeaways.what_they_do: They scope permissions down to specific agents/people and add guardrails to prevent catastrophic actions or runaway API bills.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to have permissions that are scoped down to specific agents and specific people... or to a $10,000 API fee

takeaways.technique: Design harness features as removable primitives, hide internals to iterate faster
takeaways.what_they_do: They build composable primitives so features can be added/removed without refactors, and expose less of the harness internals to users to reduce change-management drag.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you have primitives, you can add new features without making things more complicated for the agent, and you can remove features without having to do a complicated refactor
